events.title: Miller wins
events.text: Zell Miller won a special election for the Senate, the last Democratic Senate win in Georgia until 2021.

events.title: Perdue elected governor
events.text: Sonny Perdue became the first Republican elected governor of Georgia since Reconstruction.

events.title: Chambliss unseats Cleland
events.text: Saxby Chambliss (R) beat Senator Max Cleland (D), 52.8 to 45.9 percent.

events.title: A Republican House
events.text: Republicans won the Georgia House for the first time since Reconstruction; they had taken the state Senate after 2002.

events.title: Majority rule restored
events.text: The legislature restored the rule that a general-election winner needs more than half the vote.

events.title: The margin narrows
events.text: Georgia voted Republican for president by 5.2 points, down from 16.6 in 2004.

events.title: Collins loses a runoff
events.text: Mike Collins, a trucking-company owner from Jackson, lost the Republican runoff for the 10th district House seat.

events.title: The 6th district
events.text: Jon Ossoff lost a special House election runoff in the Atlanta suburbs to Karen Handel, 48.2 to 51.8 percent.

events.title: Kemp edges Abrams
events.text: Brian Kemp (R) beat Stacey Abrams (D) for governor by 1.4 points, the closest governor's race since 1966.

events.title: Biden by 11,779
events.text: Joe Biden carried Georgia by 11,779 votes, the first Democratic presidential win there since 1992.

events.title: No majority
events.text: In the Senate race, David Perdue led Ossoff 49.7 to 48.0 percent, short of a majority: a runoff.

events.title: Ossoff wins the runoff
events.text: On 5 January Ossoff beat Perdue, 50.6 to 49.4 percent.

events.title: Warnock wins too
events.text: The same day Raphael Warnock beat Senator Kelly Loeffler; the two wins gave Democrats control of the Senate.

events.title: Sworn in
events.text: On 20 January Ossoff, 33, became Georgia's first Jewish senator.

events.title: SB 202
events.text: A new election law shortened general-election runoffs from about nine weeks to four.

events.title: Prison abuse inquiry
events.text: Ossoff's Senate investigations subcommittee reported sexual abuse of women in federal prisons.

events.title: Ticket splitting
events.text: Kemp won re-election by 7.5 points on the same day Warnock led the Senate race.

events.title: Warnock re-elected
events.text: Warnock beat Herschel Walker in the December runoff, 51.4 to 48.6 percent.

events.title: Collins elected
events.text: Collins won Georgia's 10th district House seat, east of Atlanta.

events.title: Laken Riley Act
events.text: Collins's House bill, named for a nursing student killed in Athens in February, passed the House 251 to 170.

events.title: Prison Oversight Act
events.text: A prison oversight law written by Ossoff and Republican Mike Braun was signed on 25 July.

events.title: Trump carries Georgia
events.text: Donald Trump won Georgia by 2.2 points, carrying 132 of its 159 counties.

events.title: Riley Act becomes law
events.text: The Senate version of the Laken Riley Act, which Ossoff voted for, was signed on 29 January.

events.title: “Bow to no king”
events.text: On 22 March Ossoff opened his re-election campaign at a rally in Atlanta.

events.title: Collins runs
events.text: On 27 July Collins entered the Republican primary for the Senate.

events.title: Kemp backs Dooley
events.text: Governor Kemp endorsed Derek Dooley, a former football coach, in the Republican primary.

events.title: Hyundai raid
events.text: On 4 September a federal immigration raid at the Hyundai battery-plant site near Savannah detained 475 people.

events.title: Ethics referral
events.text: On 7 October a House ethics office referred Collins to the Ethics Committee over an intern's pay; its review continues.

events.title: Shutdown ends
events.text: Ossoff voted against the deal that ended the 43-day federal shutdown on 12 November.

events.title: Primary day
events.text: On 19 May Collins led with 40.5 percent, Dooley took 30.2 and Buddy Carter 25.1; Ossoff was unopposed.

events.title: Trump endorses Collins
events.text: On 14 June President Trump endorsed Collins, two days before the runoff.

events.title: Collins wins the runoff
events.text: On 16 June Collins beat Dooley, 55.5 to 44.5 percent.

events.title: No Libertarian
events.text: In July the Libertarian Party ended its petition drive; only two names are printed on the Senate ballot.

events.title: Trump in Marietta
events.text: On 22 July President Trump held a rally for Collins in Marietta, in Cobb County.

events.title: Kemp endorses Collins
events.text: On 14 September Governor Kemp endorsed Collins.

events.title: Likely Democratic
events.text: On 23 September the Cook Political Report moved the race to Likely Democratic.

events.title: First debate
events.text: On 8 October Ossoff and Collins met in their first televised debate, in Atlanta.

events.title: Second debate
events.text: On 13 October they debated again, at the Atlanta Press Club.

events.title: Early voting
events.text: In-person early voting runs from 13 to 30 October; more than a million Georgians had voted in person by 20 October, a record for a midterm.

events.title: Election Day
events.text: On 3 November Georgians choose a senator; if no one wins a majority, a runoff follows on 1 December.

eras: A Republican state, a changing electorate
chartNote: Each state is coloured by the margin of the most recent presidential popular vote (Democratic minus Republican share of all votes; FEC certified results). It is a simplification: Georgia elects its senator in its own race, and many Georgians split their tickets (in 2022 a Republican governor won by 7.5 points on the day a Democratic senator led), so the presidential colour is a backdrop, not a forecast. Shares are of land area, not of people or votes. Boundaries are today's states (Natural Earth); the map is framed on Georgia, so outer states are cut at the edge.
